The **alcohol flush reaction** (also known as "Asian flush" or "Asian glow") is ` [Highlight start] a type of alcohol intolerance that causes skin redness and warmth—usually on the face, neck, and chest—after drinking alcohol [Highlight end] ` . It happens when your body cannot efficiently break down **acetaldehyde** , a toxic compound formed when alcohol is metabolized.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESoQEBxCJF1xl1taElbrHXL4-yRon4S6SPWc0tW249O0o1O3j7vWxeumF_pXZRl5w-nQjk--Sx2oDtAO9tlZNzZ6Pp3FEEQOaZ_C5KyN0ImHrCljZ80xgZKwwUlIFv1efPtQlxpnzNEfCjvqyz7TgxUlbnM-u8MYStX0hdhcTVahRYmMOmutvOteOk2dY1ci5Y7gqnb6s9Llt-0pOqzrijL71Now)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgwEBxCJF1zhUT4bus8CWrdzL0mu4hq87pDZlqBgsJahazvbwP2-wRAnRi8FzJVeEwKwe1PcIOS77uFeO7m-YQHkBagSeIgeltHeeOpPM1gDOcYlO-KKVwyf6yhucHGERGRhGo9DWsJkK_ac9wu1xzeQ07XykKB_RejLZMkVW4P5o01oWUg)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShgEBxCJF1z22IiDSvqIoLXCSBwduDmL8c_bvN5m3vZ3jVJf6etUAJmmwkHgQKxxpDGyDoLXR99copH_nUB780lIMhWaQhFa8jCOIhHsvJeZeI6QJiTlB8GMKizGqZnf0wx6WAA6lOhN6vEw8bJKWz3QQu4b24zSGaIEL3u8-ltjEjqd5zjTanA)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiQEBxCJF14jvKNsH9POuE621GWlOPGKHIsGZ-qWu9uJUfl8ks014fwJtp7c7czxssuCh0wK1iei1ZAqVrV_VtHaZ2PZyfM4LPJ_UpMAwX8NiQ48tNLyFiU54AQoAAa183rgwQas6J7wiXnuuSuEDxcMgKw-tXJ0MtwUricojENDWjd0Gz-zFlBoBgg)

### Symptoms

- Facial, neck, or chest redness (or skin darkening/discoloration on deeper skin tones) and warmth
- Rapid heart rate or palpitations
- Nausea or vomiting
- Headaches or migraines
- Nasal congestion or worsening asthma symptoms
- Low blood pressure or dizziness[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbwHEIkXXoDUTaPUhduANvNnarLfFpJWa7WMe-XP_CuaWDbIU04Cylpjp3UJzO5uV6CRMcr11wAWjEsn6dOr8CZCte1-Io3-eOnTAj3uaVqBPha8M6ds7j4jNcXq4lk1MwznZimQvlLRjLXzjrXg0hQ)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShgEBxCJF1z22IiDSvqIoLXCSBwduDmL8c_bvN5m3vZ3jVJf6etUAJmmwkHgQKxxpDGyDoLXR99copH_nUB780lIMhWaQhFa8jCOIhHsvJeZeI6QJiTlB8GMKizGqZnf0wx6WAA6lOhN6vEw8bJKWz3QQu4b24zSGaIEL3u8-ltjEjqd5zjTanA)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXXhGL-UqNLFutr3F1s_uNkSz86h8yjZOkwgzrrtOZ5EORic9diDzN1KW5WANxxQrX568yNJPBK10fF9v-0yibmRJRPWlAY6hVWUNCh2dXMjIZFjShPUZD-FAr7LzSFCLQRWxCcmSO2)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHEIkXXHppdBm474_rpi8qASHx7ltcZDhFNgIO2lv988Cm6sAvQK5Bu_3r3_WcKlpPfdV6INsDbSVlNQEdbuNJ6dCWH4Hlftq_zskZj3gM8UfAFYrmeRSRRj6VehRvoMy5ezQgjHQ)[[5]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiQEBxCJF14jvKNsH9POuE621GWlOPGKHIsGZ-qWu9uJUfl8ks014fwJtp7c7czxssuCh0wK1iei1ZAqVrV_VtHaZ2PZyfM4LPJ_UpMAwX8NiQ48tNLyFiU54AQoAAa183rgwQas6J7wiXnuuSuEDxcMgKw-tXJ0MtwUricojENDWjd0Gz-zFlBoBgg)[[6]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbAHEIkXXcLm2co-Qa8iXc2FtPeX-56ahMvjZGhlGpA9TpiDMndQ4u8vc0ftV77vilrEwQhKj4j65VeLecIRmBJZ1pIuNkjgzum4RDKBXR4KiLJLBUKWJPOpZY9D0XvFAlio-HjIZS1JTXiZI4w)

### Causes and Risk Factors

- **Genetics:** Most cases stem from inherited variations in genes that control alcohol-metabolizing enzymes—most notably **ALDH2** (aldehyde dehydrogenase 2) and **ADH1B** (alcohol dehydrogenase 1B). When ALDH2 works slowly, acetaldehyde builds up and triggers histamine release and blood vessel dilation.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESoQEBxCJF1xl1taElbrHXL4-yRon4S6SPWc0tW249O0o1O3j7vWxeumF_pXZRl5w-nQjk--Sx2oDtAO9tlZNzZ6Pp3FEEQOaZ_C5KyN0ImHrCljZ80xgZKwwUlIFv1efPtQlxpnzNEfCjvqyz7TgxUlbnM-u8MYStX0hdhcTVahRYmMOmutvOteOk2dY1ci5Y7gqnb6s9Llt-0pOqzrijL71Now)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiQEBxCJF14jvKNsH9POuE621GWlOPGKHIsGZ-qWu9uJUfl8ks014fwJtp7c7czxssuCh0wK1iei1ZAqVrV_VtHaZ2PZyfM4LPJ_UpMAwX8NiQ48tNLyFiU54AQoAAa183rgwQas6J7wiXnuuSuEDxcMgKw-tXJ0MtwUricojENDWjd0Gz-zFlBoBgg)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXXhGL-UqNLFutr3F1s_uNkSz86h8yjZOkwgzrrtOZ5EORic9diDzN1KW5WANxxQrX568yNJPBK10fF9v-0yibmRJRPWlAY6hVWUNCh2dXMjIZFjShPUZD-FAr7LzSFCLQRWxCcmSO2)
- **Ancestry:** These genetic variants are common in people of East Asian descent (affecting roughly 30% to 50% of Chinese, Japanese, and Korean populations), though they can occur in people of any background.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESpQEBxCJF1z_Sya5RjC61Gm_sw_08SBCnpl5t9HKG69aZKAHVbAbzkJwjb2Pyx36IAjtd3S38CwFqAqGJCmRhUifwRp7m2S4bfOllcW7frLrFze7H_kWFFoApwUMcgJgK1rYIttsQOtjtbOQIPyPhbYudOVIQnXfN7AT2sap_VX-l6QO_r5TJo5yOk7pvAkBYFzMze0jOF7Uq8gSWi-kZIwoW-OaR9jE)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESoQEBxCJF1xl1taElbrHXL4-yRon4S6SPWc0tW249O0o1O3j7vWxeumF_pXZRl5w-nQjk--Sx2oDtAO9tlZNzZ6Pp3FEEQOaZ_C5KyN0ImHrCljZ80xgZKwwUlIFv1efPtQlxpnzNEfCjvqyz7TgxUlbnM-u8MYStX0hdhcTVahRYmMOmutvOteOk2dY1ci5Y7gqnb6s9Llt-0pOqzrijL71Now)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbwHEIkXXoDUTaPUhduANvNnarLfFpJWa7WMe-XP_CuaWDbIU04Cylpjp3UJzO5uV6CRMcr11wAWjEsn6dOr8CZCte1-Io3-eOnTAj3uaVqBPha8M6ds7j4jNcXq4lk1MwznZimQvlLRjLXzjrXg0hQ)
- **Medications:** Certain drugs—such as disulfiram or specific medications for infections, diabetes, or high cholesterol—can interfere with alcohol metabolism and cause a similar reaction.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESoQEBxCJF1xl1taElbrHXL4-yRon4S6SPWc0tW249O0o1O3j7vWxeumF_pXZRl5w-nQjk--Sx2oDtAO9tlZNzZ6Pp3FEEQOaZ_C5KyN0ImHrCljZ80xgZKwwUlIFv1efPtQlxpnzNEfCjvqyz7TgxUlbnM-u8MYStX0hdhcTVahRYmMOmutvOteOk2dY1ci5Y7gqnb6s9Llt-0pOqzrijL71Now)

### Long-Term Health Effects
Acetaldehyde is a known carcinogen and causes cellular stress and inflammation. People who have the alcohol flush reaction and continue to drink alcohol face a higher risk of:[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESoQEBxCJF1xl1taElbrHXL4-yRon4S6SPWc0tW249O0o1O3j7vWxeumF_pXZRl5w-nQjk--Sx2oDtAO9tlZNzZ6Pp3FEEQOaZ_C5KyN0ImHrCljZ80xgZKwwUlIFv1efPtQlxpnzNEfCjvqyz7TgxUlbnM-u8MYStX0hdhcTVahRYmMOmutvOteOk2dY1ci5Y7gqnb6s9Llt-0pOqzrijL71Now)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHEIkXXHppdBm474_rpi8qASHx7ltcZDhFNgIO2lv988Cm6sAvQK5Bu_3r3_WcKlpPfdV6INsDbSVlNQEdbuNJ6dCWH4Hlftq_zskZj3gM8UfAFYrmeRSRRj6VehRvoMy5ezQgjHQ)

- Cancers of the upper digestive tract (such as the mouth, throat, and esophagus) as well as breast cancer
- High blood pressure and cardiovascular issues
- Liver damage with regular drinking[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESewHEIkXXbsA1pwkO49EXuGIO8_XXQ5SSrKmzOIMqoZQAAEtsD14c-QJeOBaoT6-DymUJyqQcc91gBxrjGdc_iMJueE2kDRe-kD6M3YjxYFfdalZltxBiGkzE7fQ2aojum_BpBl3Zkjzh6J-bYc5dl1Zk2nlycNXd2GMW6g)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESoQEBxCJF1xl1taElbrHXL4-yRon4S6SPWc0tW249O0o1O3j7vWxeumF_pXZRl5w-nQjk--Sx2oDtAO9tlZNzZ6Pp3FEEQOaZ_C5KyN0ImHrCljZ80xgZKwwUlIFv1efPtQlxpnzNEfCjvqyz7TgxUlbnM-u8MYStX0hdhcTVahRYmMOmutvOteOk2dY1ci5Y7gqnb6s9Llt-0pOqzrijL71Now)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShgEBxCJF1z22IiDSvqIoLXCSBwduDmL8c_bvN5m3vZ3jVJf6etUAJmmwkHgQKxxpDGyDoLXR99copH_nUB780lIMhWaQhFa8jCOIhHsvJeZeI6QJiTlB8GMKizGqZnf0wx6WAA6lOhN6vEw8bJKWz3QQu4b24zSGaIEL3u8-ltjEjqd5zjTanA)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHEIkXXHppdBm474_rpi8qASHx7ltcZDhFNgIO2lv988Cm6sAvQK5Bu_3r3_WcKlpPfdV6INsDbSVlNQEdbuNJ6dCWH4Hlftq_zskZj3gM8UfAFYrmeRSRRj6VehRvoMy5ezQgjHQ)[[5]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXXhGL-UqNLFutr3F1s_uNkSz86h8yjZOkwgzrrtOZ5EORic9diDzN1KW5WANxxQrX568yNJPBK10fF9v-0yibmRJRPWlAY6hVWUNCh2dXMjIZFjShPUZD-FAr7LzSFCLQRWxCcmSO2)

### Prevention and Management
The [National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESoQEBxCJF1xl1taElbrHXL4-yRon4S6SPWc0tW249O0o1O3j7vWxeumF_pXZRl5w-nQjk--Sx2oDtAO9tlZNzZ6Pp3FEEQOaZ_C5KyN0ImHrCljZ80xgZKwwUlIFv1efPtQlxpnzNEfCjvqyz7TgxUlbnM-u8MYStX0hdhcTVahRYmMOmutvOteOk2dY1ci5Y7gqnb6s9Llt-0pOqzrijL71Now) notes that the most effective way to prevent the reaction and its health risks is to **avoid or strictly limit alcohol** . Taking antihistamines or over-the-counter remedies before drinking may hide surface redness or mild symptoms, but they do not stop acetaldehyde from building up or damaging cells.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESoQEBxCJF1xl1taElbrHXL4-yRon4S6SPWc0tW249O0o1O3j7vWxeumF_pXZRl5w-nQjk--Sx2oDtAO9tlZNzZ6Pp3FEEQOaZ_C5KyN0ImHrCljZ80xgZKwwUlIFv1efPtQlxpnzNEfCjvqyz7TgxUlbnM-u8MYStX0hdhcTVahRYmMOmutvOteOk2dY1ci5Y7gqnb6s9Llt-0pOqzrijL71Now)

### Diagnosis
Doctors typically identify the condition based on your symptom pattern after drinking, family history, and medication review. Genetic testing can confirm specific enzyme variants like *ALDH2* , though it is rarely needed for day-to-day management.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESoQEBxCJF1xl1taElbrHXL4-yRon4S6SPWc0tW249O0o1O3j7vWxeumF_pXZRl5w-nQjk--Sx2oDtAO9tlZNzZ6Pp3FEEQOaZ_C5KyN0ImHrCljZ80xgZKwwUlIFv1efPtQlxpnzNEfCjvqyz7TgxUlbnM-u8MYStX0hdhcTVahRYmMOmutvOteOk2dY1ci5Y7gqnb6s9Llt-0pOqzrijL71Now)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShgEBxCJF1z22IiDSvqIoLXCSBwduDmL8c_bvN5m3vZ3jVJf6etUAJmmwkHgQKxxpDGyDoLXR99copH_nUB780lIMhWaQhFa8jCOIhHsvJeZeI6QJiTlB8GMKizGqZnf0wx6WAA6lOhN6vEw8bJKWz3QQu4b24zSGaIEL3u8-ltjEjqd5zjTanA)Are you looking into this for yourself or someone else? Sharing **specific symptoms**, **how much alcohol triggers them** , or **any medications taken** can help tailor this information—or we can dive deeper into **cancer and cardiovascular risks** or **how it differs from an alcohol allergy**.

- **Ancestry:** These genetic variants are common in people of East Asian descent (affecting roughly 30% to 50% of Chinese, Japanese, and Korean populations), though they can occur in people of any background.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESpQEBxCJF1z_Sya5RjC61Gm_sw_08SBCnpl5t9HKG69aZKAHVbAbzkJwjb2Pyx36IAjtd3S38CwFqAqGJCmRhUifwRp7m2S4bfOllcW7frLrFze7H_kWFFoApwUMcgJgK1rYIttsQOtjtbOQIPyPhbYudOVIQnXfN7AT2sap_VX-l6QO_r5TJo5yOk7pvAkBYFzMze0jOF7Uq8gSWi-kZIwoW-OaR9jE)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESoQEBxCJF1xl1taElbrHXL4-yRon4S6SPWc0tW249O0o1O3j7vWxeumF_pXZRl5w-nQjk--Sx2oDtAO9tlZNzZ6Pp3FEEQOaZ_C5KyN0ImHrCljZ80xgZKwwUlIFv1efPtQlxpnzNEfCjvqyz7TgxUlbnM-u8MYStX0hdhcTVahRYmMOmutvOteOk2dY1ci5Y7gqnb6s9Llt-0pOqzrijL71Now)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbwHEIkXXoDUTaPUhduANvNnarLfFpJWa7WMe-XP_CuaWDbIU04Cylpjp3UJzO5uV6CRMcr11wAWjEsn6dOr8CZCte1-Io3-eOnTAj3uaVqBPha8M6ds7j4jNcXq4lk1MwznZimQvlLRjLXzjrXg0hQ)
- **Medications:** Certain drugs—such as disulfiram or specific medications for infections, diabetes, or high cholesterol—can interfere with alcohol metabolism and cause a similar reaction.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESoQEBxCJF1xl1taElbrHXL4-yRon4S6SPWc0tW249O0o1O3j7vWxeumF_pXZRl5w-nQjk--Sx2oDtAO9tlZNzZ6Pp3FEEQOaZ_C5KyN0ImHrCljZ80xgZKwwUlIFv1efPtQlxpnzNEfCjvqyz7TgxUlbnM-u8MYStX0hdhcTVahRYmMOmutvOteOk2dY1ci5Y7gqnb6s9Llt-0pOqzrijL71Now)

items.title: Prevention and Management
items.text: The National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism notes that the most effective way to prevent the reaction and its health risks is to avoid or strictly limit alcohol. Taking antihistamines or over-the-counter remedies before drinking may hide surface redness or mild symptoms, but they do not stop acetaldehyde from building up or damaging cells.
items.markdown: The [National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESoQEBxCJF1xl1taElbrHXL4-yRon4S6SPWc0tW249O0o1O3j7vWxeumF_pXZRl5w-nQjk--Sx2oDtAO9tlZNzZ6Pp3FEEQOaZ_C5KyN0ImHrCljZ80xgZKwwUlIFv1efPtQlxpnzNEfCjvqyz7TgxUlbnM-u8MYStX0hdhcTVahRYmMOmutvOteOk2dY1ci5Y7gqnb6s9Llt-0pOqzrijL71Now) notes that the most effective way to prevent the reaction and its health risks is to **avoid or strictly limit alcohol** . Taking antihistamines or over-the-counter remedies before drinking may hide surface redness or mild symptoms, but they do not stop acetaldehyde from building up or damaging cells.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESoQEBxCJF1xl1taElbrHXL4-yRon4S6SPWc0tW249O0o1O3j7vWxeumF_pXZRl5w-nQjk--Sx2oDtAO9tlZNzZ6Pp3FEEQOaZ_C5KyN0ImHrCljZ80xgZKwwUlIFv1efPtQlxpnzNEfCjvqyz7TgxUlbnM-u8MYStX0hdhcTVahRYmMOmutvOteOk2dY1ci5Y7gqnb6s9Llt-0pOqzrijL71Now)
